location.hint: Jenny uses your phone's GPS to know where you are: the recent position is injected into context each message, a precise fix only on request. Requires the Android location permission. Locations shared via Telegram apply there only and expire after an hour.

ssh.title: SSH
ssh.hint: Jenny can run commands on the machines you register here. Every host is added by hand: the agent can only name an alias you already declared, never an arbitrary address.
ssh.aliasHint: The only name Jenny uses for this host. It cannot be changed later.
ssh.authHint: A key is installed once on the server and can be revoked on its own, without touching the password you log in with. A password is more convenient and weaker: it is stored in config.json, not encrypted.
ssh.passwordPlaceholder: The password of that user on the server
ssh.passwordHint: Stays on the phone, inside config.json, like the Telegram token and the API keys.
ssh.passwordKeepBlank: Leave blank to keep the saved one.
ssh.passwordRequired: A password is required to save a host that authenticates with a password
ssh.fieldsRequired: Alias, host and user are required
ssh.credentialsLost: SSH access to {aliases} has to be set up again. The private key and the verified fingerprints deliberately live outside the workspace, so they are not in the backup and a restore cannot bring them back: regenerate the key, install the public one on the server and accept the fingerprint again.
ssh.noKeyYet: Generate the key, then install it on the server.
ssh.regenerateConfirm: Regenerate the key for {alias}? The one already installed on the server will stop working.
ssh.publicKeyHint: Paste this line into ~/.ssh/authorized_keys on the server. The private key stays on the phone.
ssh.fingerprintIntro: Compare this fingerprint with the one on {alias} before accepting it. From now on Jenny will only talk to the machine that presents it.
ssh.fingerprintPasswordWarning: This host authenticates with a password: on the first command that password is handed to whichever machine presents this fingerprint. If it isn't yours, you gave it to them. With a password this step matters more than with a key, not less.
ssh.verifyCancelled: Fingerprint not accepted: the host stays unverified
ssh.changedWarning: {alias} is presenting a host key different from the one you accepted. It may be a reinstalled server, or someone sitting in the middle. Accept only if you know why it changed.
ssh.replaceConfirm: Replace the accepted fingerprint for {alias}? If you did not reinstall the server yourself, this is what an attack looks like.
ssh.deleteConfirm: Delete host {alias}? Its key and accepted fingerprint are deleted too.

update.availableCritical: Security update available: version {version}. Worth installing right away.
update.restarting: Installation started: Jenny will restart on her own shortly. The connection will drop and come back by itself, nothing for you to do.
update.promptNote: The last step is yours: Android has to ask you before it replaces the app. If you can't see its screen, the request arrived as a notification — open it and confirm there. If you already dismissed it, you can press "Install now" again.
update.checkUpToDate: No update: you already have the latest version.
update.checkFailed: I couldn't reach the update server.
update.neverChecked: The first update check hasn't run yet.
update.stale: Since then the checks start but never reach the server: the last one that worked is still the one from {when}. While that lasts, you wouldn't hear about a new version.
update.staleNever: No successful check on record. If it stays that way after a "Check now", the mechanism isn't working and you wouldn't hear about a new version.

battery.title: Background activity
battery.hint: Without a battery optimization exemption Android suspends Jenny while the screen is off: scheduled work, reminders and proactive checks arrive late or not at all.
battery.otaHint: A system update may have reset the battery optimization exemption. Without it, scheduled work and reminders start slipping again: worth turning it back on.
battery.granted: Exemption active: scheduled work, reminders and proactive checks keep running with the screen off.

keepAwakeCost.off: Best battery life, but scheduled work and reminders can slip by hours.
keepAwakeCost.turns: Wakes the processor for a turn, a cron job or an SSH command, then releases it: costs nothing at rest.
keepAwakeCost.always: Nothing ever slips, but it drains battery constantly: it makes sense for a phone on charge.

battery.keepAwakeHint: The exemption tells Android not to throttle Jenny; this choice decides whether Jenny keeps the processor awake herself. With the screen off the CPU suspends and timers stop firing.
battery.keepAwakeRestart: The new choice takes effect at the next Jenny restart: the service-lifetime lock is taken once, at startup.
battery.keepAwakeSaved: Saved — active from the next Jenny restart
battery.exactAlarmsHint: Android does not grant the exact alarm permission on its own: without it, it batches Jenny's wake-ups with other apps' and scheduled work, reminders and proactive checks arrive minutes — sometimes an hour — late.
battery.exactAlarmsRestart: Alarms already queued stay inexact even after the permission is granted: they go back to the exact minute from the next Jenny restart.
battery.exactAlarmsFailed: The permission screen could not be reached on this phone.
battery.diagUnavailable: Diagnostics are not available right now.
battery.gapsHint: An outage is a stretch of at least {minutes} minutes when Jenny was not running: reminders, scheduled jobs and proactive checks did not fire during that time.
battery.gapsEmpty: No outage recorded: Jenny stayed up.
battery.oemHint: The outages above are not a Jenny fault: the phone's battery manager shuts her down while the screen is off. No line of app code can prevent it — the restriction has to be lifted by hand, in the manufacturer's own settings.
battery.oemOpenFailed: No battery management screen could be reached on this phone.
